sections.h2: Where does Branch County record deeds and mortgages?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds for Branch County sits in the Courthouse Annex at 23 East Pearl Street, Coldwater. Counter service runs 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday with no midday closure, and the phone is 517-279-4320.

Anything received at or after 4:30 is stamped with that day's date and goes on record the next morning, so a late delivery does not lose its priority. E-recording is accepted, which suits lenders and title agents closing a Coldwater, Bronson or Quincy sale from a distance. Frequent researchers can pay monthly for remote access, and occasional ones pay per search.

An owner checking for back taxes before listing can use the treasurer's free delinquent tax search at bsaonline.com. Under Online Services choose Delinquent Tax Search, then enter a surname, a parcel number or a street address.

sections.h2: What does the Branch County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
The flat charge is $30 per instrument, however long it is. Of each fee, $4 is routed to the state's survey and remonumentation fund, except on fixture filings, state and federal liens, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers. The fee schedule itself is in MCL 600.2567.

  • Deed, mortgage, lien notice, lien release or discharge, UCC fixture filing: $30.
  • Extra instruments covered by one assignment or discharge: $3 apiece.
  • Recorded copy: $1 a page; certified copy: another $5 per document.
  • Index search: 50 cents for every year covered, minimum $5; tax lien search: $3 per name.
  • Fax or email of a document: $5.

Enclose a stamped return envelope with mailed paper, because the office needs it to send the recorded original back.

sections.h2: Why would Branch County reject a deed?
sections.html:
Most returns trace to the format rules in MCL 565.201. Run through this list before you submit.

  • Under every signature, print or type the signer's name, and sign in black or dark blue ink. The spelling must match the notary's block.
  • Print the notary's name on the same page, close to the notary's signature.
  • Give every grantee's mailing address, and the drafter's name and business address.
  • Leave 2 1/2 inches blank at the top of the first page and half an inch around the rest.
  • Open with one line naming the single recordable event, such as a warranty deed.
  • Use black ink at 10-point or larger on white 20-pound paper, sized from letter to legal.
  • Blank out the first five digits of any Social Security number, and attach an English translation to foreign text.

Once a document meets these tests, the register cannot refuse it over what it says.

sections.h2: Does a Branch County deed need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
It depends on the type of deed. A warranty deed, any deed carrying a covenant of warranty, a land contract, and a land contract memorandum with a warranty clause must be accompanied by a certificate from the Branch County Treasurer. MCL 211.135 is the source, and it looks for two findings: no tax liens or tax titles on the parcel, and all taxes paid for the five years preceding the instrument.

The treasurer bills $5 per document covering up to five descriptions, then 20 cents for every description after that. Pay it by a separate check to the Treasurer's Office, not on the recording check.

Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants are outside the rule, which is why a family transfer or a title cleanup often moves faster. A seller who owes back taxes should expect the warranty deed to wait until the balance is cleared.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Branch County sale cost?
sections.html:
Two taxes apply. The county levies 55 cents on each $500 of value or fraction (MCL 207.504), and the state adds $3.75 on the same unit (MCL 207.525). That makes $4.30 per $500, or $8.60 per $1,000. Either the deed shows the full value on its face or a valuation affidavit rides along.

The Register of Deeds collects it on transfers of $100 or more and posts a schedule on its resources page. The purchase agreement decides which party pays.

A median-priced Branch County house therefore generates roughly $1,400 in combined transfer tax.

sections.h2: Which Branch County transfers escape transfer tax?
sections.html:
The county and state exemption lists are close but not identical. Both skip papers with consideration below $100, security instruments, leases, court orders with no stated price, boundary corrections, quitclaims that merely confirm title, and land contracts that have not yet passed legal title.

  • Only the state act, MCL 207.526, exempts a person's conveyance to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild, step-grandchild or adopted grandchild.
  • The state act also covers any mortgage foreclosure deed or deed in lieu. The county act, MCL 207.505, limits that to loans made, guaranteed or insured by a government.
  • Because the county list has no entry for gifts to children, ask the Coldwater office whether the 55 cents still applies to a family deed.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Branch County?
sections.html:
Coldwater serves as county seat and largest city of Branch County, which was created in 1829 and organized in 1833. At 520 square miles it ranks third-smallest in Michigan by total area. Bronson is the second city, Quincy, Sherwood and Union City are villages, and sixteen townships make up the balance. Agriculture remains the base of the local economy, and the Coldwater micropolitan area takes its name from the seat.

The 2020 Census counted 44,862 people, and the 2025 estimate stands at 45,993 across 506 square miles of land, about 88.6 per square mile. Of the 21,287 housing units, 77.7% are lived in by their owners. Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $162,500, rent for a typical unit is $959, and 16,906 households report a median income of $63,724. Poverty touches 13.2% of residents and 21.1% are 65 or older. The mean commute is 22.7 minutes.

Against a U.S. median home value of $332,700, those prices mean the recording fee, the tax certificate and the transfer tax weigh heavily on a Branch County closing statement.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Branch County?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document regardless of page count. A single assignment or discharge covering several instruments adds $3 for each extra one, and a warranty deed needs a separate treasurer certificate starting at $5.

faqs.q: Where is the Branch County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is in the Courthouse Annex at 23 East Pearl Street, Coldwater, open 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. Call 517-279-4320.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Branch County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register of Deeds takes e-recordings, and any paper received at 4:30 p.m. or later is stamped that day and recorded the next morning.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed in Branch County need a tax certificate?
faqs.a: Generally no. MCL 211.135 leaves out a quitclaim or other conveyance without a covenant of warranty. Warranty deeds and land contracts do need the county treasurer's certificate.

faqs.q: Is a deed to my child taxed in Branch County?
faqs.a: Not by the state, which exempts conveyances to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild under MCL 207.526(j) and (k). The county act lists no matching exemption, so confirm the county's 55 cents per $500 with the Register of Deeds before recording.
